chunks: From him, from Al-Haysam Al-Nahdi, from Abdul Aziz ibn Umar, from one of his companions, from Yahya ibn Imran Al-Halbi, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Which of the characteristics is the most beautiful for a man?' He said: 'Dignity without awe, generosity without seeking recompense, and preoccupation with that which is not the chattels of the world.'

key_terms.مَتَاعِ الدُّنْيَا: chattels or goods of the world

ai.seo_question: What are the most beautiful characteristics of a believer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the ideal character of a believer through three balanced traits: dignified composure without intimidation, generosity without expectation of reward, and detachment from worldly trinkets. This teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on *Wasālah* (spiritual connection) and *Zuhd* (asceticism), where inner peace and sincerity (*Ikhlas*) are prioritized over social status or material accumulation. The description aligns with the concept of the *Mumin* whose heart is anchored in the eternal, rendering him free from the anxiety of worldly loss.
